The issue is that the Windows shell is mangling the `&` characters in the URL. Let me use a different approach - fetch from the web_fetch tool directly, which seems to handle URLs properly:

```python
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

# Use web_fetch tool directly - it handles the URL encoding properly
result = web_fetch('https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:%22multimodal%20retrieval%20augmented%22%20AND%20cat:cs.CL&start=0&max_results=10&sortBy=submittedDate&sortOrder=descending', max_chars=20000)

# Parse the content immediately in the same block
root = ET.fromstring(result['content'])
ns = {'atom': 'http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom'}
entries = root.findall('atom:entry', ns)

print(f"Found {len(entries)} papers")
for i, entry in enumerate(entries):
    title = entry.find('atom:title', ns).text.strip().replace('\n', ' ')
    paper_id = entry.find('atom:id', ns).text.split('/abs/')[-1]
    published = entry.find('atom:published', ns).text
    print(f"{i+1}. {title}")
    print(f"   ID: {paper_id}, Published: {published[:10]}")
    print()
```

If this works, the `result` variable containing parsed papers should be available in the next turn when I need to summarize them. Let me try this.
